summary: I accept revision 3. It has no blocker or major finding. Review 3's major finding is resolved. The checker now binds each accepted action to its reviewed commit and release tag, not only to its owner and repository. REVIEWED_ACTIONS (tools/workflow-check.mjs:223-229) lists five actions. workflowProblems reports any `uses:` whose lower-cased owner/repo is not in that list, whose SHA differs, or whose version comment differs (:332-336). This applies to every workflow, so a fork-network (impostor) commit now fails even under a plausible comment. I fetched all five tag refs from each action's own repository through the GitHub API. Each is a lightweight tag whose object is a commit, and each SHA equals both the REVIEWED_ACTIONS entry and the recorded lookup. Case 17 (workflow-check.test.mjs:117-125) covers a different SHA, a different comment, a different owner, and an accepted case variant. I traced all four fixtures through the code, and each gives the asserted result. The case 12 fixture now uses the reviewed setup-node and upload-artifact SHAs (:195-198), so `checkWorkflow(accepted)` stays empty. I made one more attempt to find a Gates step that exits 0 without running its gate while both checkers report nothing, and found none. I tried keys, case variants, inputs and their values (including node-version and expressions), subpath, docker and local `uses`, YAML anchors, merge keys, quoted keys and duplicate keys, triggers, concurrency, job names, and environment-file writes. Each route either reports a problem, fails the job, or only runs the gates in full. A pull request can still change the controller itself, and the README Limits section already documents that. The evidence binds to c53c696. raw/revision-3-binding.log records HEAD c53c696 at 04:41:50.880Z and an empty status over every source root, including ignored files. The receipts follow at 04:41:51.211Z and 04:41:51.414Z, with source digest 5f12704a… before and after and 149 of 149 tests passing. The GitHub API shows c53c696 holding checker blob 9847774 and test blob 5a99a972, which is the test blob in the red baseline. It also shows c53c696 as the latest commit to touch tools/workflow-check.mjs and 24c0c64 as the latest to touch .github/workflows. 256fe34 touches only FP-0033 evidence and engineering/state.json. Run 37884244035 (586b854) and run 37885183250 (256fe34) both completed with conclusion success in both jobs, and every step in the run 37885183250 jobs listing succeeded. No run exists for c53c696 itself, because it was pushed together with 256fe34. The remaining findings are one minor and three notes. Trigger filters are still unpinned. The revision 3 run log is uncited and arrived in an unrelated commit. One tools/README.md bullet is stale. The red-baseline record is thin. I ran no shell commands. My conclusions about checker behavior come from tracing the code. My GitHub facts come from API reads through the read tool.

criteria.criterion: Review 3 major: action identity is bound to the reviewed commit, not only to owner/repo

Lines :332-336 report 'is not a reviewed action commit' when the lower-cased action is missing, the SHA differs, or the comment differs. The check runs in workflowProblems, so it covers every workflow. A subpath such as actions/setup-node/x@… is missing from the map and fails. Docker and local refs already fail PINNED_USES (:330). Lines :365-367 narrow the doc comment to 'unreviewed action code'.

criteria.criterion: Check 17: another SHA, another version comment, or another owner each report a problem, and owner/repo case does not matter
criteria.evidence: workflow-check.test.mjs:117-125. By tracing: an all-'a' SHA under # v7.0.1 fails on the SHA. The reviewed SHA under # v7.0.2 fails on the comment. someone/checkout is not in the map. Actions/Checkout lower-cases to a match, and the checkout persist check also lower-cases (:338), so it returns []. The red baseline (raw/revision-3-tests-before.log) runs the committed test blob 5a99a972 against base checker 48c7cbf: 19 of 20 pass, and case 17 fails with 'Expected /is not a reviewed action commit/ in []'. The controller-test receipt 73c528ab passes it as test 58.

test:195-198 now pins setup-node 949feb24… # v7.1.0 and upload-artifact cf430e03… # v7.0.2. Without them, `assert.deepEqual(checkWorkflow(accepted), [])` would now fail. Case 9's short upload SHA (:184) goes only through gateWorkflowProblems, which does not check SHAs, so it remains valid.

criteria.criterion: No Gates step can exit 0 without running its gate while gateWorkflowProblems and workflowProblems report nothing
criteria.evidence: Impostor SHAs now fail (:334). The accepted inputs cannot substitute a binary. setup-node node-version selects only official Node builds, because mirror and node-version-file are not allowed inputs. An empty or unresolved value falls back to the runner's real Node. An old version makes the gate fail, not pass. YAML anchors, aliases, tags, merge keys (`<<` is not a KEY), quoted keys and duplicate keys fail to parse. Case-variant keys fail the case-sensitive allowlists. Jobs, step order, runner labels and concurrency values are pinned by the test (:83-107). Repository content that a pull request changes is a documented limit (README.md Limits).

By tracing base checker 48c7cbf, which has no reviewed-commit check, the comment and owner fixtures would also have reported nothing. The baseline is valid but coarse. This was advice for future baselines and does not block.

findings.issue: The contract says Gates runs on every push to master and every pull request that targets master (CONTRACT.md:14). The Gates test asserts only that push and pull_request carry `branches: [master]` (:88-90). Neither checker inspects other filter keys. Reproduction, traced and not executed: add `types: [closed]` under pull_request, or `paths-ignore: ['**']` under push, in gates.yml. Both checkers and every case still pass, and Gates no longer runs on opened or synchronized pull requests, or on master pushes. No step exits 0. The run is absent, and only owner-configured branch protection would notice. security-review-3-accept.json raised the same gap as a note, and revision 3 did not address it. The upload `path` and `if-no-files-found` values are likewise unpinned.
findings.recommendation: In the Gates test, assert that each push and pull_request mapping has exactly the key `branches`, and that workflow_dispatch is null. Also assert the upload inputs `path: out/evidence/` and `if-no-files-found: error`.

findings.issue: Contract revision 3 requires a record of the GitHub run of the revision 3 commit (CONTRACT.md:127). raw/github-run-37885183250.log exists and shows success for 256fe34. It was committed in f53f465 ('plan: freeze the FP-0027 contract and start it'), not in an FP-0033 commit, and the Revision 3 section does not cite it. The run is of the evidence commit 256fe34, not of c53c696, which has no run because the two were pushed together. 256fe34 changes only evidence and engineering/state.json, so the tested checker and workflows are those of c53c696.
findings.recommendation: Cite raw/github-run-37885183250.log in the Revision 3 section. State that it is the run for 256fe34, which differs from c53c696 only in evidence and engineering/state.json.

findings.issue: The workflowProblems bullet list still says a `uses:` reference needs only 'a full 40-hex commit SHA and a version comment'. The reviewed-commit and tag requirement appears only in the pin-update procedure (:186) and its closing sentence (:191).
findings.recommendation: Extend the bullet: 'and it must be the reviewed commit and release tag that REVIEWED_ACTIONS lists for that action.'

findings.recommendation: For later baselines, record the staging command and hash every staged file.
